source.title: Recognition-Refusal Misalignment in LLMs: Why Models Answer Structurally Unanswerable Questions

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the reported findings.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends the safety-refusal direction to structural unanswerability: it compares that direction with an impossibility-recognition direction and intervenes on the latter. Structural-invalidity abstention is a different behavior from refusal of harmful user requests, so the results do not directly test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study measures geometry involving the canonical harmful-minus-harmless safety-refusal direction, but does not ablate or add that direction to test harmful-request refusal. Its interventions steer a different direction and measure invalidity-aware responses to structurally impossible questions. Those behavior results are recorded under fits_no_version, not assigned to a claim version. Omitted layer-selection values and individual probe values shown only in figures; the 48-cell deterministic sweep is not comparable to the intervention-grid metric and the paper says it supports no per-cell claim.
record.test_reason: The study builds the Arditi harmful-minus-harmless direction only as a comparator for its own structural-impossibility direction. It never ablates or adds that direction, and never measures harmful-request refusal rates, capabilities, jailbreaks, weight edits or multi-direction structure. All causal steering uses d_imp and measures invalidity-aware abstention on impossible math and code prompts, which is a different behaviour. The record's 'tests/T3' contradicts its own reasoning that no listed version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased. Models linearly encode structural impossibility before generation, but this signal is near-orthogonal to the Arditi safety-refusal direction. Steering along it causally changes invalidity-aware behaviour on math and code, and the geometry predates instruction tuning. The failure is therefore one of routing, not encoding, scoped to structural impossibility.
record.recipe_differences: The study constructs the safety-refusal comparator using the harmful-minus-harmless MeanDiff recipe and behavior verification, but does not intervene on that direction. Its causal steering uses a distinct answerability direction, derived in an A-null subspace, and evaluates invalidity-aware behavior rather than harmful-request refusal.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported geometry depends on subspace: same-space A-null cosine remains low, while full-space cosine is larger and attributed largely to shared A-PC variance. Intervention outcomes vary by model, dataset, direction and dose; the study also reports sensitivity to the invalidity-aware labeling rubric, mixed-output and degeneration guards, and gate size.

fits_no_version.finding: A one-dimensional A-null MeanDiff direction detects structural impossibility (mean AUC 0.939 across 22 cells; 0.977 in base models).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structural-impossibility information is linearly accessible in a single residual-stream direction before generation.

fits_no_version.finding: The impossibility direction is near-orthogonal to the safety-refusal direction (matched cosine 0.087; same-space 0.097). The full-space 0.240 is mostly shared A-PC variance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structural-impossibility recognition and the canonical safety-refusal direction are distinct axes.

fits_no_version.finding: A behaviour-defined invalidity-aware direction is partially aligned with d_imp (0.40) and near-orthogonal to d_ref,safety (0.08).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Invalidity-aware abstention on impossible prompts is not carried by the safety-refusal direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering along d_imp shifts invalidity-aware behaviour on math and code relative to random directions (+7 to +52pp, varying by model and direction), dose-responsively in Mistral code A→U.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A structural-impossibility direction causally controls invalidity-aware abstention, with model- and direction-dependent effects.

fits_no_version.finding: Strict refusal language appears on 0/50 impossible prompts in every one of the eight cells.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models rarely use standard refusal phrasing for structurally impossible prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: The low d_imp–d_ref cosine is already present in base models (mean Δcos +0.037).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Separation of impossibility recognition from the safety-refusal direction predates instruction tuning.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, pp. 24766–24794 (2026)
record.problems: The authors state that the intervention grid is only four anchors, and that Qwen3-8B intervention cells use candidate-label passthrough without second-pass overrides. Labels are LLM-assisted rather than fully human-adjudicated, and the paper reports material changes from mixed-output handling, degeneration guards, and gate broadening. The 48-cell breadth sweep uses a different, non-comparable metric and is not a per-cell intervention effect estimate. General capability preservation is not evaluated. Base/instruct comparisons include a proxy safety-refusal direction for Llama-3.1-70B-Base and a Qwen2.5-32B substitution for an unavailable Qwen3-32B base.
record.rows_left_out: Individual per-cell cosine values plotted in Fig. 2 are not all stated numerically in the text, so the aggregate cosine findings are recorded rather than figure-read estimates. The 48-cell steering breadth sweep is omitted because the paper states its hallucination-reduction metric is not comparable to the gated signal-minus-random intervention metric and supports no per-cell claim. Fact800 dose results and transfer-boundary evaluations are omitted because they concern a distinct epistemic-unanswerability setting and do not test a listed claim version.

untested.parts: No ablation or addition of d_ref,safety and no harmful-refusal or capability measure. Behaviour verification (20/22 cells pass) is mentioned but not reported quantitatively.
The Appendix L k=5/10 subspaces compare refusal with impossibility, not refusal's own dimensionality.
No separation of harm judgment from the refusal decision.
d_ref is not compared across base and instruct models, languages or variants; only its cosine with d_imp is.
Training is not varied; base/instruct contrasts concern d_imp–d_ref geometry only.
No reasoning models; explicitly left to future work.

record.verdict_notes: Changed relation from tests/T3 to uses_without_test/T4. d_ref,safety serves only as a comparator, so no version gets a verdict and the empty labels are kept. Incidental detail a researcher might note: d_ref behaviour verification passed in 20/22 instruct cells, with Llama-3.1-8B needing a proxy. Llama-3.1-70B-Base refuses too rarely to behaviour-verify, which is loosely relevant to V7 but is not measured. All rows correctly carry versions ['none'].

versions.untested_parts: Does not ablate or add the harmful-minus-harmless direction to measure harmful-request refusal or general capabilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration evaluation.
No jailbreak suppression of the safety-refusal direction or robustness training against its ablation.

The study compares separate directions for structural-impossibility recognition, invalidity-aware behavior, and safety refusal; it does not test whether the harmful-refusal mechanism itself is affine, conic, or multi-directional.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgments and harmful-request refusal decisions.
Base/instruct comparisons measure geometry between recognition and safety-refusal directions, not transfer of the same direction across languages or model variants.
Does not vary refusal-training method or timing to test when a removable refusal direction exists.
No reasoning-model evaluation; the authors leave explicit reasoning-mode training to future work.
